item.title: Setting timing windows from the risk at a site
item.description:
In our last post , we introduced timing windows for in-water work and the Timing Windows Calculator, which we built with the Centre for Ecosystem Management to identify periods of lower risk for fish populations in a lake or a river. We closed on its main limit: it looks at when fish spawn, migrate, and rear, and at nothing else.

In this post, we look at what it would take to go further. We explain how a window is scored, what changes when the score is built from the risk fish face at a site rather than from fish timing alone, and what the data available today already allow.

item.title: Scoring timing windows for in-water work
item.description: Dredging, shoreline construction, culvert replacement, dam removal, reef building: in-water work cannot always be avoided, but its timing can usually be chosen to minimize the impacts it will have on wildlife. This is usually achieved through the identification of optimal timing windows for in-water work. They set the periods when work may proceed around the fish it could harm, or the restricted periods when it may not, so that life cycles crucial for the health of populations, such as spawning, migration, and rearing, are avoided.
